entry_cohort.description: The repository's existing split: patients ordered by their FIRST encounter_id, 60/20/20. Sorts patients by entry cohort, not encounters by time. This is the setup every current headline number came from.

random.description: NEGATIVE CONTROL. Patients assigned to train/val/test uniformly at random, same proportions, same patient-level grouping. No drift exists by construction, so any signal that fires here is mis-calibrated.

temporal.description: TRUE TEMPORAL SPLIT, newly defensible because Phase 0.1 verified chronological ordering against external clinical/regulatory anchors. ENCOUNTERS are cut chronologically at the 60th and 80th percentiles of encounter_id. Patients appearing in an earlier split are removed from the later split, so the evaluation is leakage-free and reads as "train on everything up to time T, evaluate on patients first seen after T".

interpretation.negative_control_result: Under a no-drift random split the detector fires 0.25 +/- 0.55 of 8 signals on average; severities {'NONE': 16, 'MILD': 4}, alert statuses {'STABLE': 20}.
interpretation.required_statement: Any signal firing under random splitting is detector mis-calibration, not evidence of drift. The original 8/8 CRITICAL result must be discounted by exactly this baseline.
